findings.proposedIrEvidence: Rule ir-rule:888dded0b9bf82818855591e has posture PERMISSION, sufficiency COMPLETE, and only one condition: "The aggregate fair market value (determined as of the date such Lien is incurred) of the assets subject to such Liens must not exceed the greater of $50,000,000 and 3.0% of Consolidated Total Assets (measured on the date of incurrence of such Liens), tested on a consolidated basis as to the Parent Borrower and all Subsidiaries". No condition references the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the obligations secured by the Liens, and no "neither...nor" conjunction is represented.
findings.sourceEvidence: (m) Liens not otherwise permitted by this Section 7.3 so long as neither (i) the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the obligations secured thereby nor (ii) the aggregate fair market value (determined as of the date such Lien is incurred) of the assets subject thereto exceeds (as to the Parent Borrower and all Subsidiaries) the greater of (A) $50,000,000 and (B) 3.0% of Consolidated Total Assets (measured on the date of incurrence of such Liens);
findings.verifierReasoning: The source section 7.3(m) permits Liens only if both limbs of the "neither...nor" condition are satisfied: (i) the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the secured obligations does not exceed the greater-of threshold, and (ii) the aggregate fair market value of the assets subject to the Liens does not exceed that same threshold. The proposed IR encodes only limb (ii) and marks the resulting rule as a COMPLETE PERMISSION. A concrete divergence is easy to construct: a Lien securing $60,000,000 of obligations over collateral with fair market value of $10,000,000 would satisfy the IR's only condition if the threshold is $50,000,000, but it would violate the real source because the principal amount exceeds the threshold under limb (i). The IR therefore overstates the capacity/permission available under 7.3(m). This is material because a reviewer using the IR could reach the wrong compliance conclusion.

No condition references the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the obligations secured by the Liens, and no "neither...nor" conjunction is represented.
findings.sourceEvidence: (m) Liens not otherwise permitted by this Section 7.3 so long as neither (i) the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the obligations secured thereby nor (ii) the aggregate fair market value (determined as of the date such Lien is incurred) of the assets subject thereto exceeds (as to the Parent Borrower and all Subsidiaries) the greater of (A) $50,000,000 and (B) 3.0% of Consolidated Total Assets (measured on the date of incurrence of such Liens);
findings.verifierReasoning: The source section 7.3(m) permits Liens only if both limbs of the "neither...nor" condition are satisfied: (i) the aggregate outstanding principal amount of the secured obligations does not exceed the greater-of threshold, and (ii) the aggregate fair market value of the assets subject to the Liens does not exceed that same threshold. The proposed IR encodes only limb (ii) and marks the resulting rule as a COMPLETE PERMISSION. A concrete divergence is easy to construct: a Lien securing $60,000,000 of obligations over collateral with fair market value of $10,000,000 would satisfy the IR's only condition if the threshold is $50,000,000, but it would violate the real source because the principal amount exceeds the threshold under limb (i). The IR therefore overstates the capacity/permission available under 7.3(m). This is material because a reviewer using the IR could reach the wrong compliance conclusion.

A concrete divergence is easy to construct: a Lien securing $60,000,000 of obligations over collateral with fair market value of $10,000,000 would satisfy the IR's only condition if the threshold is $50,000,000, but it would violate the real source because the principal amount exceeds the threshold under limb (i). The IR therefore overstates the capacity/permission available under 7.3(m). This is material because a reviewer using the IR could reach the wrong compliance conclusion.
